issues.description: The delimiter argument conflates literal characters with OpenAPI symbolic style names in one keyword.
issues.detail: Callers can pass either a raw character ('|', ',', ' ') or a style name ('pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited') through the same parameter, mixing two vocabularies. The _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS dict also conflates identity mappings with alias mappings. A cleaner shape is a set of allowed chars plus a small alias map, or a typed Enum.

issues.description: Unsupported-delimiter ValueError is undocumented and may surface to clients as HTTP 400.
issues.detail: The new precondition raises ValueError mid-request, but the Raises clause only mentions HTTPBadRequest. Because get_param_as_list converts ValueError from transforms into HTTPBadRequest, a programmer error (bad delimiter) risks being reported as client error. Either document the exception, use a distinct exception type for the developer-contract violation, or validate at the boundary.

issues.description: Silent no-op when delimiter is set but the value arrived as an already-parsed list is surprising.
issues.detail: If upstream parsing produced a list (multiple instances), delimiter is silently ignored. A caller asking for pipe-splitting may get list members containing unsplit pipes. Documented in a Note, but the postcondition becomes runtime-type-dependent. Either split list elements too, reject the combination, or make the no-op explicit in code with rationale.

issues.description: Stringly-typed delimiter API would be clearer as a typed Enum or Literal union.
issues.detail: Symbolic names like 'pipeDelimited' are magic strings validated at runtime. An Enum or Literal would let the type checker enforce the contract and avoid future collisions (e.g., a new single-char delimiter conflicting with a style name). Not load-bearing, but aligns the API with its actual shape.

issues.description: Missing test: delimiter set with an absent param should return the default.
issues.detail: No test exercises get_param_as_list with delimiter provided and the param missing, so the postcondition for that branch is unverified. A small test would lock the contract that delimiter has no effect when the param is absent.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature is small, well-scoped, and the implementation is mostly data-driven. The shared concern is the delimiter parameter: it complects literal characters with OpenAPI symbolic style names through a single dict that also conflates identity with alias mappings — cleaner as a set of allowed chars plus a small alias map or a typed Enum. Two contract issues stand out: the ValueError on unsupported delimiter is undocumented and risks being converted to HTTP 400 for what is really a programmer error, and the silent no-op when the value arrived as a list weakens the postcondition. Test coverage for the missing-param-with-delimiter branch is the remaining gap.
